title: States
text:
Explore state-by-state support across presidential administrations from Harry Truman to Donald Trump. title: Background
text:
Put simply, a presidential approval rating is the percentage of people who approve and are satisfied with the job of the current president and their administration.
Approval ratings were first collected in 1938 by George Gallup as a way to use newer and more accurate polling methods to analyze how people felt about sitting president, Franklin D. Roosevelt. This polling gave the public, as well as the administration, a deeper examination of public sentiment beyond just election night outcomes.

title: About
text: This page has been combined into the main Story page.

title: Story
text: How do Americans view their leaders, and how does public sentiment toward the White House compare to attitudes toward Congress and political parties? By analyzing monthly Gallup polling data from 1945 to 2026, we can track how public approval, congressional approval, and party favorability interact across various presidential administrations.

title: Story
text:
About
This project was developed for a deeper and more thorough examination of approval ratings and how they evolve over time. It examines historical trends in American political sentiment using monthly polling series from Gallup.

Data Sources:

Presidential job approval ratings (1945–2026) via Gallup and the American Presidency Project.
Congressional job approval ratings (1974–2025) via Gallup Historical Trends. Note: some graphs may not include congressional approval data prior to 1974 due to limited availability.
Party favorability ratings (1992–2025) via Gallup. Note: some graphs may not include party favorability data prior to 1992 due to limited availability.

Interactive Exploration: To view individual administration trends with month-by-month animations from Harry Truman to Donald Trump (Second Term), visit the Exploration page.
